---
title: "Make a speed ramp"
description: "Use Clip ▸ Speed Ramp… to speed up or slow down part of a clip in one step, with a choice of four shapes."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

**Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** makes a whole [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) in one step. Pick a shape and a rate, and the sheet adds the Speed actions for you. The clip keeps its start and its length, and plays more or less of its file.

<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…" tools="add_speed_ramp" />

## Make a ramp

<Steps>

1. Select one clip. **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** is available only when exactly one video or audio clip is selected. It has no keyboard shortcut.

2. To ramp part of the clip, set an [in and out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) inside it first. See [The span](#the-span).

3. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**.

4. Choose a **Shape** and a **Rate**. For **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**, choose a **Hold** too.

5. Read the [readout](#the-readout), then choose **Apply**.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="13b-speed-ramp-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Speed Ramp sheet, with Shape set to Speed Dip, Rate 0.5 beside a Presets menu, Curve set to Ease In Out and Hold set to 50%. The readout below says Speed Dip, the whole clip, from 00:00:00:00 to 00:00:05:07, then ×1 to ×0.5, held 2.63 s, back to ×1. Cancel and Apply sit at the foot, with the range ×0.1 to ×1000 to their left."
/>

**Apply** adds the actions as one undo step named after the shape, such as **Speed Dip**. When captions move with it, the step's name adds "and Re-time Captions".

The result is ordinary Speed actions, one for **Ramp Up** and **Ramp Down** and two for **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**. They show as bands on the action lane and you can [edit them by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/) like any other action.

## The span

The ramp covers the timeline's in and out range if that range lies entirely inside the clip. Otherwise it covers the whole clip, and an in and out range that runs past either edge of the clip is ignored.

The [readout](#the-readout) says which one you've got.

## The shapes

| Shape | What it makes | Rate must be | Default rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Ramp Up** | One action over the span, rising from the current rate to your rate and holding it after. | Above the rate where the span starts | ×2 |
| **Ramp Down** | One action over the span, falling to your rate and holding it after. | Below the rate where the span starts | ×0.5 |
| **Speed Dip** | Two actions: a ramp down to your rate at the start of the span, a hold, and a ramp back to the starting rate at its end. | Below the rate where the span starts | ×0.5 |
| **Speed Burst** | Two actions: a ramp up to your rate at the start of the span, a hold, and a ramp back to the starting rate at its end. | Above the rate where the span starts | ×2 |

"Up" and "down" describe the rate where the span starts, not time. That rate is the clip's own rate, or the rate an earlier Speed action ended on, so a ramp can't start slow and rise to the clip's own rate. For that, set the clip to the slow rate first, then use **Ramp Up**.

**Speed Dip** is the default because it plays less of the file, so it fits a clip that already uses its whole file. Anything that rises past the starting rate needs footage beyond the clip's current end. If a clip has none spare, trim its end first.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Shape** | One of the four shapes above. Choosing a shape resets **Rate** to that shape's default. | Speed Dip |
| **Rate** | The rate the ramp reaches, from ×0.1 to ×1000. **Presets** offers 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× and 100×, the same as the Speed sheet. | ×0.5 for Speed Dip |
| **Curve** | How each new action eases: **Ease In Out** or **Linear**. | Ease In Out |
| **Hold** | For **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**, how much of the span stays at your rate: **None**, **25%**, **50%** or **75%**. Dimmed for **Ramp Up** and **Ramp Down**, which hold nothing. | 50% |

The sheet opens on these defaults every time.

With **Hold**, the rest of the span is split evenly between the two ramps, each rounded down to whole frames and at least one frame long. On a 6-second span at 50%, each ramp takes 1.5 s and the rate holds for 3 s. At **None** the two ramps meet.

## The readout

The sheet tries the ramp on every change, including each keystroke in **Rate**, and shows what it would make.

The first line gives the shape and the span in timecode, such as `Speed Dip · the whole clip 00:00:02:00 – 00:00:08:00`. It says `the range` instead when the ramp covers the in and out range.

The second line gives the rates, such as `×1 → ×0.5, held 1.50 s, → ×1`. If the ramp can't be made, the second line gives the reason instead and **Apply** is unavailable.

## When Apply is unavailable

Nothing changes in any of these cases. The readout gives the reason, and it can include clip and action numbers and times in ticks, at 600,000 ticks to the second. The checks run in this order, so fixing one can show the next.

| The problem | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The span overlaps an action already on the clip. This counts any action, including one that would sit inside a dip's or burst's hold. The reason names it, and it's never replaced. | Set an in and out range clear of the action, or [move or remove](/speed/build-a-ramp/#move-and-resize-an-action) it. |
| A **Speed Dip** or **Speed Burst** span is shorter than two frames. | Widen the in and out range. |
| The rate is on the wrong side of the starting rate, such as a **Ramp Up** to a rate that isn't faster. | Change **Rate** or **Shape**. The reason gives the starting rate. |
| The clip is linked to its detached sound. | Choose [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| The ramp would [play past the end of the file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file). | Use the largest rate that fits, which the reason names, or trim the clip's end. |

## Good to know

- Taking a clip with sound past ×12 asks once first, on the sheet. **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the ramp, and **Cancel** leaves the sheet open. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
- Captions on a Captions track are re-timed in the same step. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).

## With an agent

`add_speed_ramp` isn't tied to the in and out range. It takes its span directly, and with no span it covers the whole clip. It can also use any action curve and any hold from 0 to 90%. A span running past the clip's end isn't accepted, which can't happen from the sheet. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

## Related

- [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/)
- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/)

---
title: "Build a ramp by hand"
description: "Add Speed actions yourself, set each one's rate and curve, and move, resize, split or remove them."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Building a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) by hand gives you full control of each change of speed, where it starts, how long it takes and how it eases. Use it when the four shapes in [Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) don't fit.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['The action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section ▸ Rate']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action', 'remove_action']}
/>

## Build a ramp

<Steps>

1. Select the clip and put the playhead where the change of speed should start.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>), or the **+** in the action lane's header. The new action is 1 s long, uses the **Linear** curve, and is selected.

3. [Move or resize](#move-and-resize-an-action) its band so it covers the change, and [set its curve](#set-the-curve).

4. In the Clip tab's **Speed** section, [set **Rate**](#set-the-rate) to the rate this action should end on.

5. Repeat for each change of speed. Each action starts from the rate the last one ended on.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="10d-clip-speed-action.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with an action selected. The action lane reads Actions 1, editing 1, with one green band, a white rate line rising across it, and a row below for the action's start, its length of 1.00 s, its curve set to Linear and a trash button. Further down, the Speed section shows Rate at 2.00× with now 1.50× in orange beside it, and a Clear button in its header."
/>

**Add Action** is available when a selected clip is under the playhead. An action needs a full second free, so Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector if it would run past the clip's end or overlap another action. Move the playhead earlier, or clear the way.

## Set the rate

While an action is selected, the **Speed** section edits that action rather than the clip.

- **Rate** shows the rate the action ends on. Type a rate from ×0.1 to ×1000, or pick 0.5, 1, 2 or 4 from its menu. Doing this turns any action into a Speed action.
- If the action doesn't set a rate, **Rate** shows the rate the clip is playing at there.
- The orange **now** beside the field shows the rate at the playhead, when that differs.
- There's no **Reset** while an action is selected. To end the action at ×1, enter 1.
- **Clear** in the section header, the × on the row when you hover over it, and **Remove from action** in the row's right-click menu all take the rate out of the action. The action stays. Clearing a rate is one undo step, and it can't be done if the clip would then [play past the end of its file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file).
- **Keep pitch** still sets the clip's own setting.
- **Fit to** belongs to the clip and can't be set inside an action, so its row is marked ⊘.

A rate too high for the file isn't accepted, and the reason at the foot of the inspector names the largest that fits. Setting a rate above ×12 on a clip with sound [asks first](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

## Set the curve

The curve is how an action eases from its starting rate to its end rate. Select the action and choose from **Curve** in the action lane's detail row, under the band:

| Curve | How the rate moves |
| --- | --- |
| **Linear** | Steadily, from start to end. This is what a new action uses. |
| **In** | Slowly at first. |
| **Out** | Slowly at the end. |
| **In Out** | Slowly at both ends. |

Changing a curve changes how much of the file the ramp reads, so it can be turned down for playing past the end of the file. The undo step is **Action Curve**.

## Move and resize an action

Drag the middle of a band on the action lane to move it. Drag either end to resize it. The grips are the outer 5 pt of a band, and they show when you hover over a band wider than 15 pt.

Bands drag the same way on the timeline and in the Clip tab's lane. A drag snaps to whole frames and stops at the next action and at the clip's end. An action can't be shorter than one frame.

You can also type in the detail row: the first field is where the action starts, measured from the clip's start, and the second is its length.

The undo steps are **Move Action** and **Resize Action**. Captions over the clip move in the same step, which adds "and Re-time Captions" to the name. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).

Moving or resizing a Speed action changes how much of the file the clip reads. If a drag would take the clip past the end of its file, the band stays at the last place that fits. If a typed value would, nothing changes and the reason names the latest clip end that fits.

## The playhead selects the action

With one clip selected, playing or scrubbing into an action selects it. The Speed section then edits that action. Clicking a band also selects it, and parks the playhead at the action's end so the preview shows the rate you're setting.

An action stays selected when the playhead moves out of it, until the playhead enters another action or you go back to the clip. So check the lane's header before you change **Rate**. It reads "editing" and the action's number while an action is selected.

## Back to editing the clip

Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or choose the **Clip** chip at the left of the action lane. The Speed section edits the clip itself again.

The playhead can stay inside the action, and it won't be selected again until the playhead leaves and comes back.

## Remove an action

Select the action and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, or choose the trash button in the detail row. With an action selected, <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the action and not the clip. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

A Speed action can't be removed if the clip would then read past the end of its file, which happens when the action was slowing the clip down. The reason at the foot of the inspector names the latest clip end that fits.

The undo step is **Remove Action**, or **Remove Action and Re-time Captions** when captions move.

## Split inside an action

A split inside a Speed action keeps the picture continuous at the cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. Each half gets its own Speed action, and the second half starts at the rate the clip had reached.

Two things can change, depending on the curve:

- With **Out** or **In Out**, the rate can jump at the cut.
- With **In** or **In Out**, the second half can end on a different frame of the file.

## Good to know

A clip linked to its detached sound can't have its Speed actions changed until you choose [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

## Related

- [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/)
- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [The Speed section](/speed/speed-section/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

---
title: "Sound at high speed"
description: "Why a clip goes silent above ×12, what the alert asks before it happens, and how ramps count towards the limit."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A clip that plays faster than ×12 loses its sound in the preview and in the export, while its picture keeps playing. Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip there.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…', 'Clip ▸ Retime Range…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…']}
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', 'The ⌥ rate stretch on the timeline']}
  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'set_action_end', 'retime_range']}
/>

## Sound is left out above ×12

The limit is the same with [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) on or off. At exactly ×12 the sound still plays, and at anything faster it doesn't. The picture carries on to the top of the speed range, ×1000.

The limit is fixed, and no setting changes it. It sits a margin below the speeds at which an export with sound can stall.

Nothing is deleted. Bring the clip back to ×12 or below and its sound returns.

## The alert

Before an edit takes a clip with sound from ×12 or below to above ×12, an alert asks first. For one clip it reads:

> “Interview” will be silent at ×16.
>
> Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The picture still plays.

For several clips it counts them. It reads “3 clips will be silent at ×16.”, or “3 clips will be silent at their new speeds.” when their rates differ, and then “Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The pictures still play.”

The alert is a question, not a block. You can always go ahead.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Set Speed** | Makes the edit exactly as you asked. It's the default button, and it keeps this name when the edit is a ramp or a stretch. |
| **Cancel** | Changes nothing and adds no undo step. |

You're asked once. A clip that's already above ×12 isn't asked about again, even if you make it faster still. A clip whose sound is switched off, or whose file has no sound, isn't asked about at all.

## Where the alert appears

| You're using | If you choose **Cancel** |
| --- | --- |
| **Clip ▸ Speed…** | The sheet stays open. |
| **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** | The sheet stays open. |
| **Clip ▸ Retime Range…** | The sheet stays open. |
| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | The sheet stays open. |
| The [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/): **Rate**, its quick picks, **Keep pitch**, **Reset** or **Fit to** | The fields go back to what they showed. |
| The [⌥ rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) | The clip stays as it was before the drag. |

A stretch is put back when you let go, so nothing has changed while the question is up. **Set Speed** then applies it again.

Moving, resizing or removing an action can't raise the rate a clip names, so those edits never ask.

## Ramps and the ×12 rule

On a [ramped clip](/speed/speed-ramps/), Frame Job looks at the fastest rate the clip names anywhere. If any rate in the ramp is above ×12, the whole clip is silent, not only the fast part.

The alert counts the ramp's peak rate in the same way. A clip at ×1 with one Speed action ending at ×16 is asked about at ×16.

An end rate on an action lying past the clip's end still counts, even though that part never plays. If a trimmed clip has gone silent for no clear reason, look for one on its [action lane](/motion/action-lane/).

## The silent audio note

The Speed section shows **Audio is silent above ×12** while a selected clip is past the limit. It needs a clip whose file has sound and whose sound is on. It appears in either pitch mode, and a ramp counts by its fastest rate.

## Good to know

- A clip that only has sound follows the same rule, and is silent above ×12.
- Clips inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) count too.
- Turning a clip's sound back on while it's above ×12 doesn't bring up the alert, because the speed didn't change. The silent audio note shows instead.
- When Speed Up Typing runs by itself after a [recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/), there's nothing to ask you with. A speed-up that would silence a clip isn't made, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector.

## With an agent

An agent is never asked. Its edit goes through, and the answer says which clips went silent. If nothing crossed the limit, the answer doesn't mention it. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

## Related

- [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/)
- [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/)

---
title: "Speed ramps"
description: "What a speed ramp is, how Speed actions build one, how to read it on the timeline, and why a ramp can't play past the end of its file."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A speed ramp changes a clip's rate over time. It can play at ×1, speed up to ×4 over half a second, hold there, and slow back down, all inside one clip.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…', 'Clip ▸ Add Action']}
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['The action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section']}
  tools={['add_speed_ramp', 'add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action', 'remove_action']}
/>

There are two ways to make one:

- [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/) with **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**, which builds a whole ramp in one step.
- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/), one change of speed at a time.

Both give you the same thing, so you can start from the sheet and adjust the result by hand.

## Speed actions

A ramp is made of Speed actions. A Speed action is an ordinary [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip's action lane whose end sets a rate. Each one:

- starts from the rate the clip is playing at when the action begins, which is the clip's own rate or the rate an earlier Speed action ended on
- moves to its own end rate along its curve
- keeps that end rate after it finishes, until the next Speed action

So a ramp up and back down is two actions. The first ends at ×4, the clip stays at ×4 after it, and the second ends at ×1.

An end rate can be anything from ×0.1 to ×1000. Only a video or audio clip can have one, because only those have a file to read at a rate.

## A ramped clip keeps its place

A ramp changes how much of the file plays, not where the clip sits. The clip's start, its end and every clip around it stay put.

Speeding part of a clip up makes it play further into its file. Slowing part of it down makes it play less of the file.

For example, take a 10-second clip at ×1 with a Linear ramp up to ×4 from 2 s to 2.5 s, and back to ×1 from 4 s to 4.5 s. It still takes 10 seconds on the timeline, but it now plays 16 seconds of its file.

This is the difference from [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), where the clip gets longer or shorter.

## Never past the end of the file

Because a ramp can play further into the file, it can run out of file. A ramp may never play past the end of the clip's media, so an edit that would do that isn't made, and the reason says what would fit.

| What you tried | What the reason names |
| --- | --- |
| Setting an end rate too high | The largest end rate that fits, to 0.001. If no rate down to ×0.1 fits, it names the latest clip end that would fit at ×0.1. |
| Moving, resizing or removing a Speed action, or clearing its rate | The latest clip end that fits |
| Applying **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** | The largest rate that fits, or that no rate fits |

Nothing changes when this happens. Frame Job beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, starting "Refused:". It stays there until you click it or the project changes. In the Speed Ramp sheet the reason appears in the [readout](/speed/make-a-ramp/#the-readout) and **Apply** is unavailable. Dragging a band doesn't show a reason. The band stays at the last place that fits.

A reason gives a clip end as a position on the timeline, in ticks, at 600,000 ticks to the second. To use one, trim the clip's end to that time, which leaves the ramp room to read.

## The rate line

A white line across the action lane draws the clip's rate over its length, higher where it plays faster and lower where it plays slower.

The line is scaled from the clip's own slowest rate to its fastest, so a gentle ramp draws as tall as a steep one. Use it to see the ramp's shape. For the figures, see the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/).

The line shows at the **Medium** and **Large** track heights and in the Clip tab's lane. A clip whose rate never changes draws no line. While the line is drawn, a selected Speed band leaves out the curve it would otherwise show.

The clip's filmstrip and waveform follow the ramp too.

## The band label

At the **Large** track height, a Speed action's band on the timeline is labelled `speed`. A band's label lists everything its action changes, so one that also changes the clip's scale reads `scale, speed`. At **Medium** it shows only its number, and at **Small** it's a plain bar.

## Good to know

- A clip linked to its detached sound can't change its speed. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
- Going above ×12 anywhere in a ramp silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/#ramps-and-the-12-rule).
- Sound on a ramped clip is rendered in the background, so a clip can be briefly silent after you edit it. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/).
- Captions over a ramped clip follow the ramp. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).

## Related

- [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/)
- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/)
- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)
- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)

---
title: "Make a speed ramp"
description: "Use Clip ▸ Speed Ramp… to speed up or slow down part of a clip in one step, with a choice of four shapes."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

**Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** makes a whole [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) in one step. Pick a shape and a rate, and the sheet adds the Speed actions for you. The clip keeps its start and its length, and plays more or less of its file.

<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…" tools="add_speed_ramp" />

## Make a ramp

<Steps>

1. Select one clip. **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** is available only when exactly one video or audio clip is selected. It has no keyboard shortcut.

2. To ramp part of the clip, set an [in and out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) inside it first. See [The span](#the-span).

3. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**.

4. Choose a **Shape** and a **Rate**. For **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**, choose a **Hold** too.

5. Read the [readout](#the-readout), then choose **Apply**.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="13b-speed-ramp-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Speed Ramp sheet, with Shape set to Speed Dip, Rate 0.5 beside a Presets menu, Curve set to Ease In Out and Hold set to 50%. The readout below says Speed Dip, the whole clip, from 00:00:00:00 to 00:00:05:07, then ×1 to ×0.5, held 2.63 s, back to ×1. Cancel and Apply sit at the foot, with the range ×0.1 to ×1000 to their left."
/>

**Apply** adds the actions as one undo step named after the shape, such as **Speed Dip**. When captions move with it, the step's name adds "and Re-time Captions".

The result is ordinary Speed actions, one for **Ramp Up** and **Ramp Down** and two for **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**. They show as bands on the action lane and you can [edit them by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/) like any other action.

## The span

The ramp covers the timeline's in and out range if that range lies entirely inside the clip. Otherwise it covers the whole clip, and an in and out range that runs past either edge of the clip is ignored.

The [readout](#the-readout) says which one you've got.

## The shapes

| Shape | What it makes | Rate must be | Default rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Ramp Up** | One action over the span, rising from the current rate to your rate and holding it after. | Above the rate where the span starts | ×2 |
| **Ramp Down** | One action over the span, falling to your rate and holding it after. | Below the rate where the span starts | ×0.5 |
| **Speed Dip** | Two actions: a ramp down to your rate at the start of the span, a hold, and a ramp back to the starting rate at its end. | Below the rate where the span starts | ×0.5 |
| **Speed Burst** | Two actions: a ramp up to your rate at the start of the span, a hold, and a ramp back to the starting rate at its end. | Above the rate where the span starts | ×2 |

"Up" and "down" describe the rate where the span starts, not time. That rate is the clip's own rate, or the rate an earlier Speed action ended on, so a ramp can't start slow and rise to the clip's own rate. For that, set the clip to the slow rate first, then use **Ramp Up**.

**Speed Dip** is the default because it plays less of the file, so it fits a clip that already uses its whole file. Anything that rises past the starting rate needs footage beyond the clip's current end. If a clip has none spare, trim its end first.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Shape** | One of the four shapes above. Choosing a shape resets **Rate** to that shape's default. | Speed Dip |
| **Rate** | The rate the ramp reaches, from ×0.1 to ×1000. **Presets** offers 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× and 100×, the same as the Speed sheet. | ×0.5 for Speed Dip |
| **Curve** | How each new action eases: **Ease In Out** or **Linear**. | Ease In Out |
| **Hold** | For **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**, how much of the span stays at your rate: **None**, **25%**, **50%** or **75%**. Dimmed for **Ramp Up** and **Ramp Down**, which hold nothing. | 50% |

The sheet opens on these defaults every time.

With **Hold**, the rest of the span is split evenly between the two ramps, each rounded down to whole frames and at least one frame long. On a 6-second span at 50%, each ramp takes 1.5 s and the rate holds for 3 s. At **None** the two ramps meet.

## The readout

The sheet tries the ramp on every change, including each keystroke in **Rate**, and shows what it would make.

The first line gives the shape and the span in timecode, such as `Speed Dip · the whole clip 00:00:02:00 – 00:00:08:00`. It says `the range` instead when the ramp covers the in and out range.

The second line gives the rates, such as `×1 → ×0.5, held 1.50 s, → ×1`. If the ramp can't be made, the second line gives the reason instead and **Apply** is unavailable.

## When Apply is unavailable

Nothing changes in any of these cases. The readout gives the reason, and it can include clip and action numbers and times in ticks, at 600,000 ticks to the second. The checks run in this order, so fixing one can show the next.

| The problem | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The span overlaps an action already on the clip. This counts any action, including one that would sit inside a dip's or burst's hold. The reason names it, and it's never replaced. | Set an in and out range clear of the action, or [move or remove](/speed/build-a-ramp/#move-and-resize-an-action) it. |
| A **Speed Dip** or **Speed Burst** span is shorter than two frames. | Widen the in and out range. |
| The rate is on the wrong side of the starting rate, such as a **Ramp Up** to a rate that isn't faster. | Change **Rate** or **Shape**. The reason gives the starting rate. |
| The clip is linked to its detached sound. | Choose [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
| The ramp would [play past the end of the file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file). | Use the largest rate that fits, which the reason names, or trim the clip's end. |

## Good to know

- Taking a clip with sound past ×12 asks once first, on the sheet. **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the ramp, and **Cancel** leaves the sheet open. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
- Captions on a Captions track are re-timed in the same step. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).

## With an agent

`add_speed_ramp` isn't tied to the in and out range. It takes its span directly, and with no span it covers the whole clip. It can also use any action curve and any hold from 0 to 90%. A span running past the clip's end isn't accepted, which can't happen from the sheet. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

## Related

- [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/)
- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/)

---
title: "Build a ramp by hand"
description: "Add Speed actions yourself, set each one's rate and curve, and move, resize, split or remove them."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Building a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) by hand gives you full control of each change of speed, where it starts, how long it takes and how it eases. Use it when the four shapes in [Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) don't fit.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['The action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section ▸ Rate']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action', 'remove_action']}
/>

## Build a ramp

<Steps>

1. Select the clip and put the playhead where the change of speed should start.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>), or the **+** in the action lane's header. The new action is 1 s long, uses the **Linear** curve, and is selected.

3. [Move or resize](#move-and-resize-an-action) its band so it covers the change, and [set its curve](#set-the-curve).

4. In the Clip tab's **Speed** section, [set **Rate**](#set-the-rate) to the rate this action should end on.

5. Repeat for each change of speed. Each action starts from the rate the last one ended on.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="10d-clip-speed-action.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with an action selected. The action lane reads Actions 1, editing 1, with one green band, a white rate line rising across it, and a row below for the action's start, its length of 1.00 s, its curve set to Linear and a trash button. Further down, the Speed section shows Rate at 2.00× with now 1.50× in orange beside it, and a Clear button in its header."
/>

**Add Action** is available when a selected clip is under the playhead. An action needs a full second free, so Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector if it would run past the clip's end or overlap another action. Move the playhead earlier, or clear the way.

## Set the rate

While an action is selected, the **Speed** section edits that action rather than the clip.

- **Rate** shows the rate the action ends on. Type a rate from ×0.1 to ×1000, or pick 0.5, 1, 2 or 4 from its menu. Doing this turns any action into a Speed action.
- If the action doesn't set a rate, **Rate** shows the rate the clip is playing at there.
- The orange **now** beside the field shows the rate at the playhead, when that differs.
- There's no **Reset** while an action is selected. To end the action at ×1, enter 1.
- **Clear** in the section header, the × on the row when you hover over it, and **Remove from action** in the row's right-click menu all take the rate out of the action. The action stays. Clearing a rate is one undo step, and it can't be done if the clip would then [play past the end of its file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file).
- **Keep pitch** still sets the clip's own setting.
- **Fit to** belongs to the clip and can't be set inside an action, so its row is marked ⊘.

A rate too high for the file isn't accepted, and the reason at the foot of the inspector names the largest that fits. Setting a rate above ×12 on a clip with sound [asks first](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

## Set the curve

The curve is how an action eases from its starting rate to its end rate. Select the action and choose from **Curve** in the action lane's detail row, under the band:

| Curve | How the rate moves |
| --- | --- |
| **Linear** | Steadily, from start to end. This is what a new action uses. |
| **In** | Slowly at first. |
| **Out** | Slowly at the end. |
| **In Out** | Slowly at both ends. |

Changing a curve changes how much of the file the ramp reads, so it can be turned down for playing past the end of the file. The undo step is **Action Curve**.

## Move and resize an action

Drag the middle of a band on the action lane to move it. Drag either end to resize it. The grips are the outer 5 pt of a band, and they show when you hover over a band wider than 15 pt.

Bands drag the same way on the timeline and in the Clip tab's lane. A drag snaps to whole frames and stops at the next action and at the clip's end. An action can't be shorter than one frame.

You can also type in the detail row: the first field is where the action starts, measured from the clip's start, and the second is its length.

The undo steps are **Move Action** and **Resize Action**. Captions over the clip move in the same step, which adds "and Re-time Captions" to the name. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).

Moving or resizing a Speed action changes how much of the file the clip reads. If a drag would take the clip past the end of its file, the band stays at the last place that fits. If a typed value would, nothing changes and the reason names the latest clip end that fits.

## The playhead selects the action

With one clip selected, playing or scrubbing into an action selects it. The Speed section then edits that action. Clicking a band also selects it, and parks the playhead at the action's end so the preview shows the rate you're setting.

An action stays selected when the playhead moves out of it, until the playhead enters another action or you go back to the clip. So check the lane's header before you change **Rate**. It reads "editing" and the action's number while an action is selected.

## Back to editing the clip

Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or choose the **Clip** chip at the left of the action lane. The Speed section edits the clip itself again.

The playhead can stay inside the action, and it won't be selected again until the playhead leaves and comes back.

## Remove an action

Select the action and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, or choose the trash button in the detail row. With an action selected, <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the action and not the clip. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

A Speed action can't be removed if the clip would then read past the end of its file, which happens when the action was slowing the clip down. The reason at the foot of the inspector names the latest clip end that fits.

The undo step is **Remove Action**, or **Remove Action and Re-time Captions** when captions move.

## Split inside an action

A split inside a Speed action keeps the picture continuous at the cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. Each half gets its own Speed action, and the second half starts at the rate the clip had reached.

Two things can change, depending on the curve:

- With **Out** or **In Out**, the rate can jump at the cut.
- With **In** or **In Out**, the second half can end on a different frame of the file.

## Good to know

A clip linked to its detached sound can't have its Speed actions changed until you choose [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

## Related

- [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/)
- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)
- [The Speed section](/speed/speed-section/)
- [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/)

<system-reminder>
Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.
